base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan food for their scout troop camping trip by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any constraints. When the user asks you to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every active participant's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm planning the food for our scout troop's weekend camping trip next month. Got any tips for feeding a group outdoors?

flow_info.value: Five scouts coming: me (troop leader), Danny, Marcus, Aisha, and Tommy
Danny was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Marcus broke out in hives after eating shrimp cocktail at the troop banquet
Tommy's mom mentioned he was recently diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes
We have about $15 per person per day for food
Marcus's mom called to correct me — she said it wasn't just shrimp, the allergist confirmed he's allergic to all shellfish including crab, lobster, and mussels
Aisha just told me she can't make it, her family has a wedding that weekend
We have a new scout joining us — Priya. Her family is Jain
Priya's dad mentioned she doesn't eat root vegetables either, like onions, garlic, or potatoes
Saturday lunch menu to check: grilled chicken skewers with garlic marinade, corn on the cob, clam chowder, gluten-free pasta with marinara sauce, and s'mores for dessert

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Danny was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye

constraints.value: Cannot eat any shellfish including shrimp, crab, lobster, mussels
constraints.surface_form: Marcus's mom called to correct me — the allergist confirmed he's allergic to all shellfish including crab, lobster, and mussels

constraints.value: Initially thought to be shrimp-only allergy based on hives reaction at troop banquet
constraints.surface_form: Marcus broke out in hives after eating shrimp cocktail at the troop banquet

constraints.value: Must limit sugar intake, needs low-sugar food options
constraints.surface_form: Tommy's mom mentioned he was recently diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes
inference_chain: Type 1 diabetes → blood sugar management required
Blood sugar management → must monitor and limit sugar/carb intake

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes)
constraints.surface_form: Priya's family is Jain. Her dad mentioned she doesn't eat root vegetables either, like onions, garlic, or potatoes
inference_chain: Jain → strict vegetarian (no meat, fish, eggs)
Jain dietary practice → also avoids root vegetables

hidden_state.value: You are a scout troop leader planning food for a weekend camping trip. You will introduce the scouts and their dietary needs, receive a correction upgrading Marcus's allergy from shrimp-only to all shellfish, lose one scout (Aisha), and gain a new one (Priya, who is Jain). At the end you will present a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, organized troop leader. You relay information from parents and scouts in third person (e.g. 'Marcus's mom called me', 'Priya's dad mentioned'). You never express frustration, even when plans change. You treat updates as normal coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

ground_truth.answer: Grilled chicken skewers with garlic marinade: problematic for Priya — chicken is meat (Jain vegetarian) and garlic is a root vegetable (Jain avoids root vegetables). Corn on the cob: fine for everyone. Clam chowder: problematic for Marcus (clams are shellfish, confirmed allergy) and Priya (not vegetarian). Gluten-free pasta with marinara sauce: fine for everyone including Danny (gluten-free). S'mores: problematic for Danny (graham crackers contain wheat/gluten — celiac) and a concern for Tommy (high sugar — Type 1 diabetes). Aisha is no longer attending so she has no constraints to consider.

Clam chowder problematic for Priya: not vegetarian

forbidden_elements: Flagging any constraint for Aisha (she is no longer attending the trip)

Over-generalizing Marcus's shellfish allergy to all seafood (e.g., saying fish is problematic for him)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint upgrade tracking and late-joining entity management. Key tracking challenges: (1) Marcus's allergy is initially presented as shrimp-only (hives after shrimp cocktail) then explicitly upgraded to all shellfish by his mother's correction — the agent must apply the broader constraint at probe time. (2) Aisha exits mid-conversation — her absence means no constraints from her apply. (3) Priya joins late as a Jain with the additional root vegetable restriction — the agent must infer Jain means no meat/fish/eggs AND remember the explicit root vegetable detail (no garlic, onions, potatoes). (4) Danny's celiac requires inferring gluten avoidance and catching that graham crackers contain wheat. (5) Tommy's Type 1 diabetes requires flagging high-sugar items like s'mores. The trap items are corn on the cob (fine — not a root vegetable, no gluten) and gluten-free pasta (explicitly safe for Danny).

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
